_comment: Laptop overfit sanity run 1 of 3 (scripts/run_overfit_tests.cmd): the real 0.6B student on ~1 s of train audio (a seeded subset of the kept reazon_small/emilia_yodas/galgame train rows; the exact ids are the `subset` events) for up to 1000 epochs = 1000 optimizer steps (step_audio_s >= the subset: one step per epoch), with an eval after every epoch on ~1 s of the pooled gate eval sets (teacher-forced + greedy) and a probe on the train subset itself (teacher-forced + greedy). Expect eval/probe/all/kl -> ~0 and eval/probe_greedy/all/cer_teacher_corpus -> 0 while the held-out eval does not improve. Early stop: once the probe KL has not improved by max(0.001, 2 %) for 20 epochs in a row (never before epoch 10) the run goes to its end phase (final eval, verdict, summary as usual; the `early_stop` event and summary.json's stopped_early say when and why). The first run of this config (overfit-1s-20260924T074759Z) memorised by epoch ~20 and its probe KL sat at ~0.01 from epoch ~80 on; this rule would have stopped it at epoch 68 (best 0.0015 at epoch 48). Otherwise the viability settings (KL 1.0, CE 0.8, L2-SP 0.05, AdamW lr 1e-4, clip 1.0, bf16 autocast, BN frozen, rel-pos patch) with SpecAugment off, the warmup capped at 10 % of the 1000 planned steps (100) and the cooldown over their last 20 % (the early stop normally comes first, without one). The 8 GB RTX 4070 holds fp32 weights + grads (4.9 GB) but not AdamW's m, v: optim.offload cpu keeps them and the fp32 masters in host memory (~12 GB RAM), updated by torch's fused CPU AdamW kernel (optim.offload_fused; the same weights as foreach within 1e-6, tests/test_overfit.py). Measured on this laptop's CPU for the 616M trainable params (two runs, both while a teacher pass was running): AdamW fused 0.5-0.6 s per step (foreach 1.2-1.6 s), the L2-SP pull + its value in one pass ~0.9-1.4 s, plus ~0.4 s of PCIe copies: ~2-2.5 s per step with the tiny forward/backward (the first run, with foreach: ~3.7 s per epoch, step and eval). Expected wall time: ~70-150 epochs x ~2.5-3 s (step + eval; ~3-8 min) + setup and smoke (~5 min) + a full state (8.6 GB, ~10-30 s) after the smoke steps and every 10 min of loop time, the resume points scripts/supervise_distill.py relaunches from after a GPU fault = about 10-15 min; without an early stop at most 1000 epochs (~45-55 min), plus ~5-10 min per crash and resume. To stop it by hand: create runs/<run_id>/STOP.
